topic: Agentic plan-to-code preflight and adversarial certification: executable acceptance criteria, simulation, negative-space review, evidence gates, human override, and regression traceability
research_questions: How do mature agentic engineering and safety systems turn plans into executable preflight checks, scenario simulations, and adversarial certification?
Which acceptance-criteria, negative-space, evidence-gate, human-override, and regression-traceability patterns are documented by primary sources?
How should a plan-to-code gate expose blocked, uncertain, overridden, and certified outcomes without conflating them?
What evidence is necessary to claim that a plan remains safe and complete as implementation and dependencies change?

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.material_relevance: Defines GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE across the AI lifecycle, including risk tolerance, trustworthiness, human-AI interaction, monitoring, and TEVV concepts for a cross-cutting assurance model.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.material_relevance: Adds GAI-specific pre-deployment and ongoing evaluation, go/no-go policies, risk-tiering, test plans, TEVV retention, red-teaming, monitoring, and deactivation or halt paths.

sources.title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1: Recommendations for Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.material_relevance: Provides outcome-focused, risk-based secure-development practices structured as practices, tasks, implementation examples, and references, with integration into automated toolchains and residual-vulnerability response.

sources.title: Run AI Red Teaming Agent Locally (Azure AI Evaluation SDK)
sources.material_relevance: Documents an automated PyRIT-backed workflow that scans model and application endpoints, simulates adversarial probing, and generates detailed reports for safety-risk discovery during design and development.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.material_relevance: Distinguishes workflows from agents and documents programmatic gates, parallel and voting reviews, evaluator-optimizer loops, ground-truth feedback, stop conditions, sandboxing, tool testing, and human checkpoints.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.material_relevance: Defines agent-evaluation tasks, trials, graders, transcripts, outcomes, harnesses, and suites, and documents multi-trial testing, unit tests, static analysis, browser tests, human calibration, and regression baselines.

sources.title: OpenAI Evals
sources.material_relevance: Provides an open-source framework and registry for evaluating LLMs and LLM systems, including custom datasets, templates, repeatable runs, and versioned eval definitions suitable for executable acceptance and regression suites.

sources.title: Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent
sources.material_relevance: Documents branch and credential limits, required human review and workflow approval, prompt-injection mitigation, CodeQL/dependency/secret scans, signed commits, session logs, and audit events for an autonomous coding agent.

sources.title: SLSA Terminology (v1.0)
sources.material_relevance: Separates recurring build-platform certification from artifact provenance verification against producer-defined expectations, providing a model for distinct process and output gates.

sources.title: in-toto Attestation Framework Spec
sources.material_relevance: Defines authenticated metadata layers for predicates, subject-bound statements, envelopes, and bundles, with a validation model intended for automated policy engines.

sources.title: Canarying Releases
sources.material_relevance: Defines canarying as a partial, time-limited deployment plus evaluation integrated into release, with representative metrics, attributable signals, pause or rollback, and human escalation.

sources.title: OpenSSF Scorecard
sources.material_relevance: Operationalizes machine-checkable security gates across CI tests, fuzzing, SAST, branch protection, code review, dependency pinning, token permissions, and signed releases, returning risk-weighted scores and remediation prompts.

findings.claim: NIST AI RMF organizes AI assurance as continuous GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE functions rather than a one-time checklist.
findings.notes: The framework describes governance as cross-cutting and the other functions as lifecycle- and context-specific risk activities.

findings.claim: A useful agent-evaluation unit includes explicit task inputs and success criteria, multiple trials, graders and assertions, a complete transcript or trajectory, and the final environment outcome.
findings.notes: Anthropic explicitly distinguishes what the agent says in a transcript from what actually exists in the environment at the end of a trial.

findings.claim: Documented agentic workflow patterns include programmatic gates between steps, parallel or voting reviews, evaluator-optimizer loops, environment ground truth, maximum iterations, sandboxing, and human checkpoints.
findings.notes: These patterns are presented as composable choices whose complexity should be justified by measurable outcome improvement.

findings.claim: Microsoft documents automated red-team scans that target model and application endpoints, simulate adversarial probing, and produce reports for safety-risk discovery.
findings.notes: The documented capability is a preview and should be treated as a pattern for repeatable adversarial testing, not as a universal certification guarantee.

findings.claim: NIST SSDF is outcome-focused and risk-based, with explicit separation of practices, tasks, implementation examples, and references, and is designed to integrate into existing automated development workflows.
findings.notes: SSDF says it is not a universal checklist; organizations select and formalize practices according to risk, cost, feasibility, and applicability.

findings.claim: GitHub's autonomous coding-agent controls combine constrained branches and credentials, required human review before merge, workflow approval, prompt-injection handling, security scans, signed commits, and session or audit logs.
findings.notes: The controls keep the agent productive while preserving a human merge boundary and traceability of agent-authored work.

findings.claim: SLSA distinguishes recurring certification of a build platform from verification that an individual artifact satisfies producer-defined provenance expectations.
findings.notes: The two verification paths provide a direct precedent for separating process health from output-specific compliance.

findings.claim: The in-toto attestation model binds authenticated metadata to a subject through predicate, statement, envelope, and bundle layers and is intended for automated policy validation.
findings.notes: The model supports evidence records that are independently inspectable and tied to a specific artifact or subject.

findings.claim: Google SRE treats a canary as a partial, time-limited deployment with an evaluation integrated into the release process, using representative and attributable metrics to decide whether to continue, pause, roll back, or contact a human.
findings.notes: The source explicitly warns that artificial test environments and nonrepresentative samples can miss defects.

findings.claim: OpenSSF Scorecard demonstrates a machine-checkable gate pattern that covers testing, fuzzing, static analysis, branch protection, code review, pinned dependencies, token permissions, and signed releases with risk-weighted results and remediation prompts.
findings.notes: The site describes execution on code updates or pull requests and reports both individual checks and an aggregate posture score.

findings.claim: For Puppet Master, the combined evidence implies that plan-to-code certification should be an evidence bundle rather than a single model judgment.
findings.notes: This is a design inference from separate task, outcome, provenance, and human-control patterns; no source specifies Puppet Master's exact schema.

findings.claim: The reviewed sources do not establish a universal numeric threshold that certifies a plan-to-code result across domains.
findings.notes: This bounded search observation is not proof that no such threshold exists; the sources instead emphasize context-specific risk tolerance, criteria, and evidence.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Lifecycle assurance is divided into GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A plan gate can expose governance, scope and risk mapping, executable measurements, and managed disposition as separate views.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Agent evaluation uses tasks, trials, graders, transcripts, environment outcomes, and a harness that aggregates results.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Acceptance criteria can be executable records with reproducible attempts and independent outcome checks.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Agentic systems use composable gates, parallel or voting reviewers, evaluator-optimizer loops, and bounded autonomous loops.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Negative-space review can be a separate evaluator lane, while deterministic checks gate each transition.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Automated red-team systems scan endpoints with adversarial probes and produce reports.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Adversarial certification can be repeatable, report-backed, and run before promotion rather than relying on informal review.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Autonomous coding changes are isolated by branch and credential limits, gated by required checks and human merge approval, and made auditable through logs and signatures.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Human override should be an explicit controlled transition with attribution, not an implicit permission hidden in agent output.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: SLSA verifies both the build platform's conformance and each artifact's provenance against producer expectations.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: A plan-to-code gate should distinguish certification of the execution lane from compliance of a specific implementation.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: in-toto composes subject-bound attestations from predicate, statement, envelope, and bundle layers for automated policy engines.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Plan constraints, test results, review decisions, and artifact identity can be represented as separately verifiable evidence.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: Canary release is partial and time-limited, compares a candidate with a control, and uses representative metrics to decide continuation or rollback.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Simulation or staged execution can produce a promotion signal while limiting blast radius and preserving rollback.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: OpenSSF Scorecard turns repository and supply-chain practices into individual checks, risk levels, an aggregate score, and remediation prompts.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: PM can present itemized evidence and risk rather than treating a single aggregate score as proof of completeness.

competitor_standard_patterns.pattern: OpenAI Evals uses a registry and reusable templates for custom, repeatable evaluations of LLMs and LLM systems.
competitor_standard_patterns.implication: Plan acceptance criteria can be versioned as reusable eval assets and rerun when models, tools, or code change.

failure_modes.failure_mode: The agent claims success in its transcript while the required environment state was not actually achieved.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Grade final environment outcomes and observable artifacts in addition to transcript assertions.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Errors compound across many tool calls and state changes in a multi-turn agent loop.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Use bounded iterations, checkpoints, intermediate gates, multiple trials, and trace capture so failures are localized and replayable.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Untrusted issue, comment, or repository content injects instructions into the coding agent's context.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Filter or isolate untrusted inputs, restrict tools and credentials to task needs, and require human approval before consequential workflows.

failure_modes.failure_mode: Generated code or newly introduced dependencies pass functional review while carrying security defects, secrets, malware, or vulnerable components.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Gate with security scanning, dependency and provenance checks, code review, signed outputs, and residual-vulnerability disposition.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A trusted or certified execution platform is mistaken for proof that a particular generated implementation satisfies the plan.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Require separate process-attestation and artifact-or-plan-expectation verification records.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A simulation or test sample is too small, unrepresentative, or disconnected from real inputs to reveal defects in a changed plan or implementation.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Record coverage assumptions, use representative scenarios and metrics, compare with a control or baseline, and stage exposure with rollback.

failure_modes.failure_mode: An aggregate score hides a critical failed check or lets a human approval become a low-information rubber stamp.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Preserve item-level results, risk severity, evidence links, reviewer identity, decision rationale, and non-waivable blockers alongside any aggregate score.

failure_modes.failure_mode: A regression is detected only after users report it because the system lacks a stable task bank, baseline, or replayable trace.
failure_modes.mitigation_or_gap: Maintain versioned eval suites, repeated trials, traces, outcome graders, and comparison against the last accepted baseline.

implications.implication: Plan-to-code assurance should emit distinct records for plan intent, preflight checks, scenario outcomes, adversarial results, artifact provenance, and human disposition.
implications.rationale: The sources treat tasks, outcomes, attestations, and process certification as different evidence objects; combining them into one opaque verdict would lose auditability.

implications.implication: Use a two-layer gate: certify the execution lane and separately verify that the produced change meets plan-specific expectations.
implications.rationale: SLSA makes this separation explicit for build systems and artifacts, while SSDF supplies a risk-based vocabulary for the expected secure-development outcomes.

implications.implication: Expose blocked, uncertain, overridden, and certified as distinct states with reasons and evidence references instead of compressing them into pass or fail.
implications.rationale: Risk tolerance, residual risk, human review, and approval controls are documented as contextual decisions rather than interchangeable success signals.

implications.implication: Every acceptance criterion should map to a machine check or named reviewer, an evidence URI, a subject or revision identity, and a freshness or invalidation rule.
implications.rationale: Subject binding, provenance expectations, and repeatable trials make evidence inspectable; freshness rules are a Puppet Master design decision derived from those patterns.

implications.implication: A certification gate must verify observable environment outcomes, not only agent messages or generated diffs.
implications.rationale: The source explicitly defines the outcome as the final environment state and warns that transcript claims can diverge from that state.

implications.implication: Negative-space review should be a separately visible adversarial suite covering untrusted inputs, tool boundaries, missing dependencies, rollback, and failure-to-stop behavior.
implications.rationale: The sources support adversarial probing, pre-deployment testing, and prompt-injection controls; the exact negative-space taxonomy is a Puppet Master inference.

implications.implication: Bind plan revision, source revision, dependency set, tool or model configuration, test environment, and produced artifact through provenance or attestations.
implications.rationale: SLSA and in-toto provide the binding and verification pattern; applying it to plan-to-code inputs is a design implication.

implications.implication: When feasible, promotion should use a bounded simulation or canary with explicit comparison metrics, a stop condition, and rollback or human escalation.
implications.rationale: Google documents staged evidence-producing rollout, while Anthropic documents bounded agent loops and environment feedback; combining them yields a plan-to-code promotion pattern.

novel_ideas.idea: Create a certification passport that is a signed, append-only evidence graph: each criterion points to its check, trace, outcome, subject hash, reviewer or automation identity, and disposition.
novel_ideas.rationale: This combines in-toto subject-bound attestations, SLSA expectation checks, and GitHub-style traceability into a plan-centric evidence surface.

novel_ideas.idea: Add a counterfactual plan simulator that executes the same acceptance suite against a baseline implementation, the candidate implementation, and deliberately injected negative cases.
novel_ideas.rationale: Baseline comparison, adversarial probes, and multi-trial outcome grading are individually documented; the combined counterfactual harness is a new proposed composition.

novel_ideas.idea: Require a negative-space budget: every certified plan records the highest-risk untested scenarios, why they are untested, who accepted the residual risk, and when they expire.
novel_ideas.rationale: NIST emphasizes risk tolerance and residual risk, while Google emphasizes test representativeness; the explicit budget and expiry are proposed governance mechanics.

novel_ideas.idea: Make overrides non-transitive: an override records exact failed criteria, bounded scope, approver, rationale, compensating controls, and expiry, and cannot silently certify later revisions.
novel_ideas.rationale: Human approval, risk tolerance, provenance expectations, and revision identity are documented separately; non-transitivity prevents a historical exception from becoming a blanket pass.

novel_ideas.idea: Use a regression replay matrix keyed by plan revision, model or tool configuration, dependency lock, environment snapshot, and trial number, so a change can be compared to the last accepted run.
novel_ideas.rationale: Anthropic and OpenAI establish repeatable evaluation and versioned suites; in-toto supplies a subject-bound evidence pattern for the replay inputs.

novel_ideas.idea: Use a dual attestation handshake: the plan emits signed expectations before execution, and the implementation emits provenance and outcome attestations after execution; certification requires both to verify.
novel_ideas.rationale: This adapts SLSA producer expectations and in-toto attestations to preserve plan intent and implementation evidence as mutually verifiable halves.

unresolved_questions.question: What domain-specific thresholds should Puppet Master use to move from uncertain to certified, and which thresholds are non-waivable blockers?
How should negative-space coverage be measured for an agentic plan when the possible tool, dependency, and environmental state space is open-ended?
What status precedence applies when automated checks pass, a human override exists, and one high-risk criterion remains unverified?
Which model, tool, dependency, environment, or policy changes should invalidate prior evidence immediately, and which can trigger a selective rerun?
How can the harness detect when an evaluator or agent exploits a loophole in acceptance criteria rather than fulfilling the intended plan outcome?
What minimum independence, expertise, and evidence review should be required for a human override in each risk tier?
Which evidence should be retained for long-term regression traceability without exposing sensitive prompts, source, credentials, or user data?
When a full canary or realistic simulation is impossible, what conservative evidence substitution is sufficient for certification rather than merely uncertainty?
